tagline: Forty-six miles of red pine, opening now and then on water.
intro: From US 2 at Deer River, Highway 46 runs northwest through the Chippewa National Forest for 46 miles to Northome. Through the stands of mature red pine the view closes in. Then it opens out onto marsh, or onto the wide water of Lake Winnibigoshish and Cut Foot Sioux, and closes in again.
The state authorized the road in 1933. By 1953 a single gravel stretch was left in the middle, and by 1958 that was paved too.

moments.title: Deer River
moments.text: The road starts at a town where, late in World War II, prisoners of war manned a logging camp nearby, on the site of an old CCC camp.

moments.title: Lake Winnibigoshish
moments.text: The Mississippi is at its widest here, more than 11 miles across where it flows through the lake, whose Ojibwe name means, more or less, filthy water.

moments.title: Cut Foot Sioux Lake
moments.text: Named for a battle fought on its shore in 1739, the lake joins Winnibigoshish through Williams Narrows, a channel 100 feet wide.
